title: Abdali Encircles Koel as the Siege Drags On

blocks.text: Even after the plan is prepared, the Muslim chiefs keep entreating Abdali to defer the assault and move on toward Agra, arguing that delay at Koel is wasteful. Abdali rejects that advice, convinced that Agra itself cannot be controlled unless the surrounding Jat resistance is first broken.

He then spreads his army around the fort from multiple directions while the defenders remain steady under Rai Mal's leadership. Fire from outside proves less decisive than hoped, water and fortifications frustrate mining, and the garrison's confidence makes the siege feel heavier with each passing day.

By this stage, seven days having been wasted, impatience and embarrassment are growing among the attackers. The page captures the sense of a campaign that is expensive, frustrating, and in need of some dramatic escalation if Abdali is to recover the initiative.
